section_summary.extract_value: This section details the participant recruitment process for a study, noting that 63,486 individuals initially responded to the Synthetic Aperture Personality Assessment (SAPA), with 3,841 of these completing the optional Creative Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ). Demographic information, including mean age (28.2 years for CAQ respondents), gender distribution, educational attainment, and race/ethnicity, is provided for the CAQ respondents and compared to the larger SAPA sample. Criteria for excluding inconsistent or uninterpretable participant data are also outlined.
section_summary.evidence_source: Participants Of the 63,486 (58% female) individuals who responded to the Synthetic Aperture Personality Assessment (SAPA) at SAPA-project.org between May 20, 2013 and June 10, 2014 in exchange for customized feedback about their personalities, 3,841 (62.2% female) completed the optional Creative Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ; Carson et al., 2005; described subsequently and included as an Appendix) after the main personality inventory. The mean self-reported age of CAQ respondents was 28.2 years (SD = 11.9, Mdn = 24) with a range from 14 to 82 years (compared with the SAPA sample: M = 25.6, SD = 10.3, Mdn = 22). Educational attainment levels for both sets of participants are given in Table 1; CAQ respondents were more highly educated than nonrespondents as indicated by the higher proportions of respondents with college/university and graduate/professional degrees. Race/ethnicity is presented for the U.S. participants (58% of the total) in Table 2. As the table shows, White/Caucasian participants represented a larger proportion of the respondent sample than the rest of the SAPA sample. Some participant data were excluded due to inconsistent or uninterpretable responses. This mainly occurred for participants who skipped all questions for one or more domains including the item that asked them to indicate if they did not have any recognized achievements in that area. Only participants who provided a response for all 10 domains were included in the analyses. Additional participant data were discarded if participants provided uncommon responses to certain demographic questions, such as an age younger than 14 or older than 90 years.
